newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says 22 arrested over bombings.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says 22 arrested over bombings.

text.p: Nigerian security agencies have arrested 22 people in connection with a recent wave of bombings in Lagos, the defence headquarters spokesman said on Wednesday.
"All the security agencies are involved in the investigation and have worked very hard because we don't want this kind of thing to happen again," Colonel Godwin Ugbo told Reuters.
He did not disclose the names of those arrested.
Lagos, centre of opposition to Nigerian military rule in Nigeria, has been rocked by three bomb attacks on military targets since December which have killed three soldiers and wounded several dozens.
The police blame the exiled wing of the umbrella opposition group NADECO for the bombings. The organisation denies any involvement.
According to the family of former finance minister and NADECO member Olu Falae he is among those arrested.
But Ugbo said "I don't know if the 22 persons include Chief Falae and I am not going to be categorising whether they are civilian or military persons, politicians or not."
"But it is something positive that the arrests have been made," he added.
He said all the suspects were arrested in the Lagos area.
Africa's most populous nation has been in crisis since 1993 when the army scrapped a presidential vote aimed at restoring democracy.
